messages.author: 7e208d26917e9ea2
messages.subject: Best methods for saving graphics?
parts:
Hello D-RUGies,

I am looking for some advice regarding the creation of publication-quality graphs in R. My graphs are simple bar charts, created using ggplot2 in R studio. I have tried writing files to various graphics devices (pdf, tiff, jpeg, etc), but the files look crappy when I open them in MS Word, even if I increase the ppi. Bitmaps look blurry and pdfs delete lines seemingly at random. Same if I save directly from the graphics window in R Studio (where they look so nice!). Copying and pasting metafiles seems to look best in Word, but I don't think publications will accept this format.

Has anyone else encountered this problem and figured out a solution?

Many thanks,
Emily

messages.author: 1ebe9f0f5834d2d6
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Best methods for saving graphics?
parts:
Hi Emily,

.pdf and .eps files are usually fine for publications because they are vector based graphics. If you make a .pdf try it with the option bg = "white" to set the background color, that may fix your disappearing lines. 

To make an eps (encapsulated post script) or a high res image  you can play around with the following commands and tweak them as you see fit:

postscript(file="Model.eps",width=6.8,height=4.5)

or

tiff(file="Model.tiff",width=6.8,height=4.5,units="in",type="quartz",res=600)

--

messages.author: 0c0915d54307a5d8
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Best methods for saving graphics?
parts:
Hi Emily,

I'm planning on giving a talk on making graphics for publication in R in a few weeks! But I havn't had the problems with pdfs deleting lines that you have had. What function do you use to export the figure? If you are using the "export plot" button, you may not be able to get the specifics you need, so I always use the "pdf" fucntion. There are equivalent functions for any other graphics formats. But as Jamie said, publications tend to specify file type and ask that figures be uploaded separately. You can also export it as an svg file and manipulate the image in Inkscape or other graphics software. (inkscape is free!)

pdf(file = "sleepplot.pdf", width= 6, height = 4, # specify width and hight in inches
    useDingbats=F) # I have had trouble when uploading figures with digbats before, so I don't use them

sleepplot2 # print our plot

dev.off() # stop making pdfs

messages.author: 1bd043dc49f3e3c4
messages.subject: Re: Best methods for saving graphics?
parts:
Just to chime in and add one quick option, "ggsave".  If you are plotting a ggplot object, you can use ggsave for most of the file types that have been mentioned. Each journal generally will have specifics for size, dpi and type and it's probably best to use the specific call for each.  However, for word docs, I think ggsave as .png's has worked well for all sorts of graphics. I've had a few little bugs here and there, but generally they are solved by using dev.off() and then rexporting.  Give it a shot.  Hope this helps.

Example:

ggsave("figure_1A.png", width=8, height=6, dpi=300)

# Or

ggsave("figure_1B.pdf", width=8, height=6)

Ryan Peek
Center for Watershed Sciences
Aquatic Ecologist
